items.title: NH투자증권 3분기 순익 3천836억…전년비 35.5% 증가

items.title: 美 제재 속 한국 생산 늘리는 ACM리서치…평택 진위 공장 증설

items.title: 유니젯, 태양전지용 SAM 잉크젯 양산장비 내년 2월 출시
items.snippet: 유니젯이 태양전지 제조공정에 쓰이는 자기조립 단분자막(SAM)을 잉크젯 방식으로 코팅하는 양산 장비를 내년 2월 출시한다. 연구개발과 파일럿 장비에서 검증한 초박막 코팅 기술을 대량생산 단계로 확대하는 것이다.유니젯은 창업주인 김석순 사장이 지난 21일부터 23일까지 독일에서 열린 '페로브스카이트 커넥트 2026'에서 SAM 잉크와 잉크젯 코팅 기술, 양산 장비 개발 현황을 발표했다고 밝혔다.SAM은 태양전지 내부에서 서로 다른 층 사이의 계면 특성을 조절하는 매우 얇은 막이다. 유니젯은 이 막을 2~3나노미터(nm) 두께로 형성하

items.title: [일렉 스타] 삼성이 투자한 우프틱스, 국내에 웨이퍼 계측장비 공급

items.snippet: 셀트리온이 26일 이사회를 열고 1천억 원 규모의 자기주식을 취득하기로 결정했다.이번에 매입하는 자기주식은 총 51만4천404주다. 주식 취득은 오는 27일부터 내년 1월 26일까지 장내 매수를 통해 진행된다.이번에 매입한 자기주식의 소각 여부는 내년 3월 정기주주총회에서 주주들의 의견을 충분히 수렴한 뒤 결정할 계획이다.주총 이후 자기주식 소각은 필요한 이사회 결의 등 관련 절차를 거쳐 확정한다.sijung@yna.co.kr

items.snippet: 김정은 북한 국무위원장이 24일 정식 개통 9일 만에 신압록강대교를 통해 중국을 방문하면서 이곳이 ‘북-중 협력의 상징’으로 다시 주목받고 있다. 특히 김 위원장이 북-중 간 육상 운송량을 크게 늘릴 수 있는 대교를 직접 통과한 것을 두고, 양국 경제협력 확대 메시지를 낸 거라는 해석이 나온다. 이 대교는 개통되기 전부터 국제 사회의 대북 경제 제재를 우회할 수 있는 통로란 평가도 받았다. 김 위원장은 이날 평양에서 평안북도 신의주까지 열차로 이동한 뒤 차량으로 갈아타고 신압록강대교를 건너 중국 랴오닝성 단둥에 도착한 것으로 전해졌다. 김 위원장은 과거 중국 방문 때 주로 전용 열차나 항공기를 이용했지만, 이번엔 최근 개통한 대교를 이용한 것. 북한 조선중앙통신은 김 위원장이 단둥의 버스 공장을 참관한 뒤 신압록강대교를 통해 중국을 떠났다고...

items.title: 김정은 전격 방중으로 ‘사망설’ 또 허위 판명
items.snippet: 김정은 북한 국무위원장이 24일 당일치기로 중국을 방문하면서 최근 일부 국내외 소셜네트워크서비스(SNS)에서 퍼졌던 ‘사망설’이 허위인 것으로 드러났다. 최근 김 위원장의 사망설이 확산된 발단은 미국에서 활동 중인 중국의 반(反)체제 인사 셰완쥔(謝萬軍)의 SNS 게시글이었다. 그는 최근 X를 통해 “김정은이 뇌출혈로 쓰러져 베이징의 한 병원으로 옮겨졌지만 결국 숨졌다”고 주장했다. 또 김 위원장의 딸 주애로의 권력 승계에 대비해 중국이 평양에 병력 수천 명을 보냈다고도 했다. 셰완쥔은 과거에도 시진핑(習近平) 중국 국가주석의 건강 이상설 등 허위 사실을 제기해온 인물이다. 이번에도 역시 객관적인 증거는 제시하지 않았다. 하지만 영국과 미국, 인도의 일부 매체들이 그의 SNS 게시물을 인용해 보도하면서 사망설은 빠르게 퍼졌다. 이에 대해, 정...

items.title: 오세훈 “총선 다가와, 통합에 최선” 2심 무죄에 야권 벌써 들썩
items.snippet: 오세훈 서울시장이 여론조사비 대납 의혹 항소심에서 무죄를 선고받으면서 야권 정치 지형이 들썩이고 있다. 오 시장은 무죄 선고 직후 ‘당 통합’을 강조하는 메시지를 냈고, 무소속 한동훈 의원도 오 시장에 대해 “힘을 합치고 함께 가야 될 분”이라고 호응하고 나섰다. 개혁신당 이준석 전 대표는 23일 오 시장의 선고가 내려지던 서울고등법원을 찾아 지원에 나서는 등 보수 야권에서는 장동혁 대표 체제를 견제하는 ‘오한석(오세훈, 한동훈, 이준석) 연대’ 가능성이 다시 주목받고 있다.● 吳 ‘통합’ 강조에 ‘오한석 연대’ 주목 오 시장은 24일 서울 여의도 국회에서 열린 한 행사에 참석한 후 기자들과 만나 “이제 총선이 다가오고 있다”며 “국민의힘이 분열된 모습보다는 단합, 통합된 모습일 때 국민 여러분께 위안을 드릴 것”이라고 밝혔다. 그러면서 “생...

items.title: 장동혁 ‘국힘 최장수 대표’… 與 “버티기 장인”
items.snippet: 장동혁 대표가 2020년 9월 국민의힘 출범 이후 ‘최장수 대표’가 됐다. 당 지도부에서는 “싸울 수 있는 정당을 만들었다”고 자평했지만 더불어민주당은 “지방선거에서 참패하고도, 사퇴 요구가 빗발쳐도 끝내 자리를 지켜 낸 버티기 장인”이라고 비판했다. 국민의힘에 따르면 장 대표는 25일로 취임 425일째를 맞이해 국민의힘 출범 이후 가장 오래 재임한 대표가 됐다. 국민의힘 대표 임기는 2년이지만 전임 대표들은 모두 임기를 채우지 못하고 중도 하차하면서 비상대책위원회가 수시로 출범했다. 당의 수장은 6년 1개월간 19번 바뀌었고 장 대표가 20번째다. 이준석 전 대표는 윤석열 전 대통령과의 갈등 속에 424일 만에 대표직에서 내려왔고 이후 김기현 전 대표가 대표직을 맡았으나 2023년 서울 강서구청장 보궐선거 패배 등으로 280일 만에 사퇴했다...

items.title: 국정원 보고뒤 “김정은, 中리창 만나”… 뒤늦게 “왕후닝으로 변경” 정정 소동
items.snippet: 국회 정보위원회 여당 간사인 더불어민주당 윤건영 의원이 24일 국가정보원의 보고를 받고 김정은 북한 국무위원장의 중국 방문 때 예정된 접견 인사가 중국 2인자인 리창(李强) 국무원 총리라고 밝혔다가 서열 4위인 왕후닝(王滬寧) 전국인민정치협상회의(정협) 주석으로 정정하는 해프닝이 벌어졌다. 국민의힘은 “대북 정보망의 수집·분석 역량에 허점이 있었던 것은 아닌지 우려스럽다”고 비판했다. 윤 의원은 24일 늦은 오후 언론 공지를 통해 “김 위원장과 중국 측 인사의 접촉과 관련하여 당초 리창 총리가 방문하는 것으로 계획되었다가 바뀐 것으로 파악되었다고 추가 보고받았다”며 “리창 총리를 만난 것이 아니라 왕후닝 주석을 만난 것으로 확인되었다고 한다”고 전했다. 정치권에서는 보안을 이유로 제한된 내용만 공개하는 정보위가 통일부 등 정부 발표에 앞서 김...

items.title: 법무장관 후보 박균택-양부남 압축, 둘 다 李변호인-檢 출신
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 법무부 장관 후보자로 더불어민주당 박균택 의원(전남광주 광산갑·사법연수원 21기)과 양부남 의원(전남광주 서을·22기)을 유력하게 검토하고 있는 것으로 알려졌다. 친명(친이재명)계인 박 의원과 양 의원은 이 대통령 사건 변호사, 검사 출신, 광주 지역 초선 의원이란 공통점이 있다. 야당은 이 대통령 사건에 대한 공소취소 모임 공동대표를 맡았던 민주당 김승원 의원에 이어 이 대통령 사건 변호에 관여한 친명계 의원들이 유력 검토되고 있는 데 대해 “돌고 돌아 대장동 변호인이냐. 이 대통령 죄 지우기 인선”이라고 비판했다.● 두 달 공백 법무부 장관 후보 모두 ‘李의 변호사’25일 청와대에 따르면 이 대통령은 정성호 전 장관이 8월 26일 퇴임한 뒤 두 달째 공석인 법무부 장관에 박 의원과 양 의원을 2배수로 압축하고 막판 고심 중...

items.title: 이태원 참사 4주기, 유가족 위로
items.snippet: 더불어민주당 김민석 대표(오른쪽)가 24일 서울 중구 서울광장에서 열린 10·29 이태원 핼러윈 참사 4주기 시민추모대회에 참석해 유가족을 위로하고 있다. 이날 행사에는 한성숙 국무총리와 남인순 국회부의장, 조국혁신당 신장식 대표 등이 참석했다.

items.title: 국감 마무리 앞둔 여야, 820조 ‘예산 전쟁’ 시작
items.snippet: 이재명 정부 두 번째 국정감사의 마무리를 앞둔 가운데 여야가 820조9000억 원으로 역대 최대 규모로 편성된 내년도 예산안 심사에서 공방을 이어갈 전망이다. 특히 예산안의 약 20%를 차지하는 미래대응기금의 신설을 두고 여야가 첨예하게 맞붙을 것으로 보인다. 국회 예산결산특별위원회는 30일 예산안 공청회를 시작으로 본격적인 예산안 심사 일정에 돌입한다. 앞서 정부가 국회에 제출한 내년도 예산은 820조9000억 원으로, 올해 본예산 727조9000억 원보다 93조 원 늘어난 규모다. 국회는 다음 달 4일과 5일 종합정책질의를 거친 다음 경제부처와 비경제부처를 대상으로 한 부별 심사를 진행한 이후 예산심사소위를 가동할 예정이다. 최대 쟁점은 반도체 호황으로 인한 추가 세수를 바탕으로 편성된 162조 원 규모의 미래대응기금이 될 것으로 보인다....

items.snippet: 조희대 대법원장 탄핵을 둘러싼 범여권 내 갈등이 격화되고 있다. 더불어민주당 김민석 대표가 “국정조사를 포함해 차근차근 진행해 가겠다”며 조 대법원장 탄핵 공식화 입장에서 한발 물러선 가운데 친청(친정청래)계와 조국혁신당은 오세훈 서울시장 2심 무죄 판결을 계기로 신속한 탄핵 추진을 요구하며 김 대표에게 공세를 펴고 있는 것. 김 대표는 24일 서울 여의도 국회에서 열린 한 행사에서 기자들과 만나 조 대법원장 탄핵과 관련해 이같이 말했다. 탄핵 여부를 곧바로 결정하기보다 국정조사를 통해 업무추진비 논란 등 사실관계를 먼저 규명한 뒤 판단하겠다는 것. 그는 16일 “모든 방법과 경로를 올려놓고 논의하기 시작했다”며 조 대법원장 탄핵을 검토하겠다는 입장을 밝힌 바 있다. 지도부는 개별 의원들과 접촉하며 조 대법원장 탄핵과 관련해 물밑에서 의견을...

items.snippet: 캐나다로 여행을 가서 대형 스키 리조트 매표소 앞에 섰습니다. 설원 위를 가르는 스키의 로망을 이루려고 큰맘 먹고 찾아왔지만, 원정 스키는 무릎 관절 부담과 낙상 사고가 늘 걱정입니다. 낮에 기온이 살짝 올랐다가 밤새 영하로 뚝 떨어졌다는데, 정상 쪽 슬로프가 꽁꽁 얼어 빙판처럼 돼 있으면 어쩌나 하는 생각에 덜컥 겁이 납니다. 리프트권을 끊기 전에 매표소 직원에게 “오늘 정상 쪽은 푹신한 자연설인가요, 아니면 딱딱하고 미끄러운 빙판인가요?”라고 물어보고 싶습니다. 그런데 막상 입을 떼려니 “Snow soft today?” “Is upper slope good snow?” 같은 엉성한 표현밖에 떠오르지 않습니다. 뒤에서 기다리는 사람들 눈치까지 보여 마음이 더 조급해집니다.

items.title: 남쪽 해상 지나는 태풍 ‘참피’… 서울은 해 쨍쨍, 포항은 배 꽁꽁

items.title: 정직 2개월 청구됐는데, 직무 정지만 6개월 넘은 박상용
items.snippet: 법무부가 ‘쌍방울 불법 대북 송금’ 사건을 수사했던 박상용 인천지검 부부장검사 직무를 정지시킨 지 6개월을 넘어섰다. 25일 기준 203일째다. 대검찰청(현 공소청)이 박 검사에 대해 청구한 징계는 정직 2개월과 견책이다. 검사징계법상 정직 최고 수위는 6개월이다. 그런데 법무부가 징계 결정을 미루면서 박 검사 직무 정지 기간이 이를 훌쩍 넘긴 것이다. 사실상 무기한 직무 배제 조치를 통해 징계를 넘어서는 불이익을 주고 있는 것 아니냐는 말이 나온다.

items.title: “진상 규명하라” 李가 지시한 사건마다 ‘무혐의’ ‘업무상 과오’
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 공소청(옛 검찰청)과 중대범죄수사청(중수청) 등 수사·기소 담당 기관 수장을 국무회의에 참석시키는 것을 두고 논란이 일자 “정당한 지휘·감독”이라고 했다. 그런데 앞서 이 대통령이 진상을 규명하라고 지시해 수사와 조사로 이어진 사건 대부분이 범죄 혐의가 없거나 일부 문제가 있어도 실무자의 착오나 업무상 과실이었던 것으로 결론 났다. 이런 일이 몇 차례 발생하자 법조계에선 “수사 가이드라인 제시 논란 등 불필요한 시비가 벌어졌다”는 말이 나온다.

items.title: ‘30년 일산’ 재건축… 용적률 350%로 올려 사업성 높인다

items.snippet: 2만2259명이 춘천의 가을을 달린다. 80주년을 맞은 ‘가을의 전설’ 춘천마라톤(조선일보사·춘천시·스포츠조선·대한육상연맹 공동 주최)이 25일 강원도 춘천시 의암호 일대에서 열린다. 풀코스 1만1932명, 10㎞ 1만327명이 도전장을 냈다. 연령별로는 30대가 8753명(약 39%)으로 가장 많고, 40대가 6605명(약 30%)으로 그 다음이다.

items.title: “잠수교 차량 금지되기 전에 달리자” 오토바이 100대 한밤 폭주
items.snippet: 서울 잠수교 차량 통행이 26일부터 전면 금지된다. 잠수교는 교각을 같이 쓰는 위층 반포대교와 마찬가지로 차량이 다니지만 보행 전용 다리로 탈바꿈하기 위해 공사가 시작되면서다. 잠수교는 용산구 서빙고동과 서초구 반포동을 잇는 길이 795m 왕복 2차선 다리다. 한강 수면과 맞닿을 듯 낮게 놓여 강물과 야경을 가까이서 즐길 수 있어 서울 주요 드라이브 코스로 꼽혀왔다.

items.title: 김치 사먹는 게 아이스크림보다 당분 섭취 많아
items.snippet: 한국인이 간식으로 섭취하는 당류(糖類)가 최근 4년 새 하루 평균 17.7g(2019년)에서 15.6g(2023년)으로 줄었다는 조사 결과가 23일 나왔다. 반면 한국인이 식사로 섭취하는 당류는 하루 평균 19g에서 19.9g으로 늘었다. 서울대 건강문화사업단(단장 윤영호 서울대 의대 교수)은 이같이 식품의약품안전처의 국민 건강 영양 조사 자료를 분석한 연구 결과를 소개했다.

items.title: Micron's next-generation 3D NAND to double bit density with over 400 layers, offering extreme performance
items.snippet: Micron's G11 3D NAND promises 42 Gb/mm2 and 5,400 MT/s interface speed, enabling SSDs with extreme capacity and performance.

items.title: 썰매의 이름은 ‘백두대간’
대통령 측근의 무능과 부패에… 청년 수만명이 죽어나갔다
items.snippet: 6·25전쟁 개전 초기 인민군은 남한 점령지역에서 20여만명의 청년을 의용군으로 강제 징집했다. 1950년 10월 국군과 유엔군이 압록강까지 밀고 올라갔던 전세가 중공군의 참전으로 역전되면서, 대한민국 정부는 미래의 병력 자원인 청년들을 후방의 안전지대로 후송할 대책을 강구했다.

items.title: 한국보다 외국서 더 인기인 ‘bojagi’
items.snippet: 지난 20일 오후 5시 서울 마포구 ‘스튜디오 보자기’. 보자기 포장 방법과 매듭 묶는 법을 배우는 ‘보자기 클래스’가 한창이었다. 미국인 제나 알콘(28)씨는 최근 보자기의 존재를 알게 된 뒤 그 매력에 빠져 어머니와 함께 수업을 들으러 왔다. 그의 어머니 엘리자베스 앳킨슨(69)씨는 “와인병 감싸는 법을 배우고 싶다”며 “크리스마스 선물 포장할 때 활용할 생각”이라고 했다.

items.title: “핑클도 완전체로?” 중년의 아이돌이 왜 자꾸 컴백할까
items.snippet: “아니, 쥬.얼.리.가 나왔어?”

items.title: 민둥산엔 은빛 억새, 함백산엔 단풍 산사… 가을 여행의 정석, 정선
items.snippet: 파란 가을 하늘 아래 은빛 억새가 산바람 따라 이리저리 군무를 추는 풍경은 오직 일 년 중 이 시기에만 볼 수 있는 진풍경 중 하나. 억새가 손짓하는 계절에 ‘민둥산은빛억새꽃축제’(~11월 8일)가 한창인 민둥산에 올랐다. 가을빛으로 물드는 태백산맥의 능선을 거닐고, 광부들의 삶이 눅진하게 녹아든 폐 탄광 박물관에서 사라져가는 산업화 시대의 초상과 마주했다. 여기에 단풍 내린 천 년 고찰과 사람 냄새 물씬 풍기는 시골 장터 구경까지, 정선이라는 소도시가 일궈온 시간을 걸었다.

items.title: 그건 사랑이 아니야 [고혜련의 삶이 있는 풍경] (27)
items.snippet: “다른 데 가서 하면 안 돼요? 보기 민망하네.” 여의도 한강가 풀밭에 앉아 쉬고 있던 어느 여름 저녁. 어둑해지자 불빛이 환해진 가로등에 기대 ‘점입가경’의 애정표현에 돌입한 젊은 남녀를 코앞에서 보고 도저히 넘어갈 수 없어 냅다 소리를 질렀다. 그들은 곧 당황한 듯 사라졌으나 얼마 후 다시 나타났다. 이번에는 의기양양한 얼굴에 반말로 “남의 일에 웬 참견이냐”며 내 가족의 어깨를 쳤다. 무언가 무장하고 왔다는 직감이 왔다. 순간 위험을 느껴 급히 움직이며 전화기로 112에 신고한 듯 외쳤다. “여기 큰일 났어요. 급히 출동해 주세요.” 그들은 움찔하며 사라졌고 위기를 모면했다는 생각이 들었다. 옆에서 “거봐, 그런 건 모른 척하는 게 상책”이라 했지만 그들에게 하고 싶은 말은 여전하다.

items.title: 가을날
items.snippet: 고등학교 시절 국어 선생님은 등단한 시인이었습니다. 선생님은 수업 시간 중 가끔 교과서에 실리지 않는 시를 소개해주셨습니다. 그때 소개받은 시 가운데 가장 기억에 남는 시가 함형수 시인의 ‘해바라기의 비명’입니다. 저의 애송시 가운데 하나가 되었습니다. 원로 문학평론가 유종호 교수님의, 시 한 편으로 1급 시인으로 평가받을 수도 있는데 함형수 시인의 경우가 그렇다는 말씀을 듣고 내 일인 양 기뻤습니다. 참 사소한 것이지만, 그것도 세상 사는 재미입니다.

items.title: 왜 아름다운 것을 멀리서만 찾았을까
items.snippet: 윌리엄 해즐릿의 에세이 제목(‘왜 먼 것이 좋아 보이는가’)대로 아름다운 것은 늘 멀리 있는 것 같다. 10월 초에 영화 몇 편을 보겠다고 부산국제영화제에 갔다. 대부분의 영화는 기다리면 차차 개봉해 동네에서 편하게 볼 수 있다는 걸 알고 있지만 꼭 그곳에서 시간표에 쫓겨가며 간신히 극장에 앉아 피곤한 몸으로 영화를 보며 축제의 일부가 되고 싶었다. 기분은 합리적인 것이 아니니까. 3박 4일 동안 나는 14편의 영화를 22시간 18분 동안 봤다.

items.title: 부의함·육개장 없애고 청바지 입고 치른 장례… 비로소 고인이 보였다
items.snippet: 송길원 목사 (아무튼주말 게재 전 사용금지)- 영상미디어 이신영 기자" height="5197" src="https://www.chosun.com/resizer/v2/7OYQHHVJNNGTTAJC6JPOBEPSW4.jpg?auth=8bdb7f9c6a6b53ed4987df69373ec26ffd491fc01ce94b23a5b4c52c83962b77&smart=true&width=3465&height=5197" width="3465" /> 지난 9월 치른 송길원(69) 목사 부친 장례식에는 다섯 가지가 없었다. 근조 화환, 부의함, 부고장, 꽃 제단, 육개장. 경기도 양평 하이패밀리센터에 차려진 빈소에서 송 목사는 검은 양복과 상주 완장 대신 흰 셔츠에 청바지를 입었다. 영정을 둘러싼 화려한 꽃 제단도 만들지 않았다. 대신 낡은 구두와 탁상시계 등...

items.title: 타코, 흑당, 감주… 다가온 호빵의 계절 입맛대로 고르세요
items.snippet: 삼립의 겨울 대표 간식 ‘삼립호빵’이 다가오는 겨울 시즌을 맞아 배우 공명을 새로운 모델로 발탁하고, ‘타코 호빵’, ‘흑당단팥·감주통팥 호빵’ 신제품을 선보이며 본격적인 겨울 마케팅에 나선다. 누적 판매량 69억개를 돌파하며 대한민국 겨울 간식의 대명사로 자리 잡은 삼립호빵은 올해 익숙한 스테디셀러의 내실을 다지는 한편, 트렌디한 감각의 신제품과 다채로운 캠페인을 앞세워 올겨울 소비자 입맛 잡기에 나섰다.

items.title: “된장찌개 1인분이요? 손님이 직접 끓이셔야 합니다”
items.snippet: 지난 17일 오후 1시 30분쯤 찾은 경기 용인의 무한리필 고깃집 ‘스타미트스타캠핑 정육식당’. 손님 7명이 점심 식사를 하고 있었다. 목살·삼겹살·LA갈비 등이 들어 있는 냉동고와 김치·마늘·양파 등 밑반찬을 꺼내 먹을 수 있는 냉장고가 비치돼 있었지만 일하는 직원은 보이지 않았다. 이 식당은 오후 9시부터 다음날 오후 4시까지는 무인(無人)으로 운영된다. 매장 안팎에는 ‘심야 무인 고깃집’ ‘계산 셀프’ 같은 종이가 붙어 있었다. 무인 운영 시간대에 손님들은 고기를 굽는 것은 물론이고 된장찌개를 끓이고 반찬을 리필하는 일도 ‘셀프’로 해야 한다. 이 업체 사장 A(52)씨는 “2년 전에 고깃집을 열었는데 직원을 하루 4시간씩 주 5일만 써도 인건비가 200만~250만원 정도라 부담이 컸다”며 “올해 3월부터 저녁 식사 시간에만 내가 상주하...

items.title: 소지품만 던져 놓고 “내 자리”… 원격 영역 표시 ‘K-자리 맡기’
items.snippet: 벤치 위에 짐짝이 한가득이었다. 먹다 만 간식에 쇼핑백, 배낭까지. 20일 오후 서울 롯데월드 복판, 물건 주인은 30분 넘게 나타나지 않았다. 사정은 뻔했다. 곧 열릴 야간 퍼레이드 공연 명당자리를 소지품으로 선점한 것이다. 한 직원이 ‘자리 맡기 금지’라고 적힌 카트를 끌고 와 물건을 담고는 분실물 보관소로 옮겼다. 그는 “아마 지금쯤 놀이기구를 타고 있을 것”이라며 “접이식 의자나 유모차 등으로 자리만 맡아 놓고 공연 직전에 와서는 점유권을 주장하는 경우가 많아 이용객 간 형평성을 위해 수거 조치를 시행하고 있다”고 말했다.

items.title: 노을이 건너는 다리
items.snippet: 어린 시절 들었던 가수 혜은이 노래에 나오는 ‘제3한강교’가 지금의 한남대교라는 건 한참 나중에 알게 됐다. 동시에 궁금해 찾아본 제1한강교는 지금의 한강대교, 제2한강교는 지금의 양화대교다. 걸어서 건널 수 있는 한강 다리 가운데 주변 전망이 좋고 걷기 편한 다리로 추천하는 게 한강대교다. 한강대교의 또 다른 매력 요소는 다리 가운데 있는 노들섬이다. 요즘은 10여개의 시내버스 노선이 지나고 있어 접근성이 크게 높아졌다.

items.title: 비싸서 마음껏 못 먹던 장어… 언제 이렇게 싸진 거지?
items.snippet: 보양식의 대명사 장어. 큰마음 먹고 지갑을 열어야 맛볼 수 있었던 외식 메뉴였지만, 최근 ‘장어 무한 리필’ ‘1인분 9800원 민물장어’를 큼지막하게 내건 식당이 우후죽순 들어서고 있다. 1㎏에 5만~7만원을 훌쩍 넘던 장어를 무제한 제공하거나, 1만원도 되지 않는 가격에 사계절 판매하는 파격적 프랜차이즈 모델이 등장했다.

items.title: Automated Multi-Line Bug Repair Using Model Checker Aided LLMs: A Case Study on RISC-V Processors
items.abstract: Functional verification of Register-Transfer Level(RTL) designs has become a critical bottleneck in modern semiconductor development, often consuming the majority of project resources. Debugging, in particular, remains an especially time-consuming task, requiring careful analysis of simulation traces or counterexamples. Recent work has explored applying Large Language Models (LLMs) to RTL debug and repair with great promise. However, the existing approaches typically are for single-line bugs, operate in open-loop, rely heavily on prompts or retrieval, lack scalability, and often produce incorrect fixes. In this paper, we propose a novel automated RTL bug repair methodology that combines LLMs, assertions, and a model checker to provide scalable, trustworthy semantic grounding and formal guarantees. items.title: Intrinsic Raman Modes and Crystal Symmetry of Altermagnetic $α$-MnTe
items.abstract: Crystal symmetry governs the physical properties of materials and provides the framework for interpreting their microscopic excitations and macroscopic responses. In altermagnets, the crystal symmetries that relate opposite-spin sublattices give rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting despite compensated magnetization. Determining the real crystal symmetry is therefore essential for understanding the intrinsic electronic and magnetic properties. For the altermagnetic semiconductor $α$-MnTe, conflicting Raman assignments have left both its intrinsic lattice excitations and its crystal symmetry unresolved. Here we combine high-resolution Raman and second-harmonic generation (SHG) spectroscopy with first-principles calculations to distinguish intrinsic lattice excitations from Te-derived spectral contributions and to examine bulk inversion symmetry of $α$-MnTe. items.title: Material criteria for angular-momentum transfer from twisted photons to photoelectrons
items.abstract: We study the material requirements for transferring the total-angular-momentum (TAM) projection of a twisted photon to the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of a photoelectron emitted from an $n$-type semiconductor surface. Within a single-valley effective-mass model of surface photoemission, we calculate OAM-resolved spectra for GaAs, InSb, $\mathrm{InAs}_{0.34}\mathrm{Sb}_{0.66}$, and $\mathrm{Hg}_{0.76}\mathrm{Cd}_{0.24}\mathrm{Te}$ irradiated by twisted photons with Laguerre--Gaussian--like momentum profile. The OAM transfer is characterized by the mean electron OAM, its root-mean-squared width, and the fraction of electrons with OAM-projection equal to the photon TAM-projection. items.title: Demonstrating RFSoC-based Control of a Fully Connected Exchange-Only Qubit
items.abstract: Semiconductor triple-quantum dots (TQDs) are a promising platform for scalable quantum information processing, but the community has so far lacked access to affordable and flexible high-speed control electronics. SpinQICK, an open-source spin qubit-control package built on the Xilinx Radio Frequency System-on-Chip (RFSoC), directly addresses this gap by leveraging the high sampling-rate signal generation and advanced digital signal processing (DSP) capabilities of the Quantum Instrumentation Control Kit (QICK) to enable precise time-domain voltage control and readout of semiconductor spin qubits. In this paper, we use spinQICK to demonstrate coherent control, state preparation, and readout of a fully connected triangular exchange-only device. items.title: Nanoscale origin of thermal anisotropy in monoclinic \texorpdfstring{$β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$}{beta-Ga2O3}
items.abstract: Monoclinic $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ is a promising ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductor for power electronics, but its low and anisotropic thermal conductivity limits heat removal, making it a compelling model system for nanoscale thermal transport studies. Here, we demonstrate a pronounced nanoscale enhancement of thermal anisotropy and uncover the underlying phonon mechanism by combining complementary thermal and acoustic spectroscopy techniques with first-principles calculations. Anisotropic thermoreflectance thermometry determines the full thermal-conductivity tensor from angular measurements within the (100), (010), and (001) crystallographic planes. Angle-resolved Brillouin light scattering reveals that low-frequency acoustic phonons exhibit only weak velocity anisotropy, insufficient to account for the measured thermal anisotropy. items.title: Structural characterization of the rutile-GeO2/TiO2 (001) heterointerface
items.abstract: Rutile-GeO2 (r-GeO2) has emerged as a promising ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) semiconductor for future high-power device applications because of its favorable combination of physical and electrical properties. This study has used high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) to compare heterointerfaces between thin films of GeO2 grown by metal-organic chemical vapor deposition on closely-lattice-matched rutile TiO2 (r-TiO2) substrates at temperatures of 840° C and 925° C. Cross-sectional TEM observations reveal interfaces with two entirely different structures: an amorphous GeOx/r-TiO2 heterostructure with an abrupt, highly faceted and non-planar interface, or a fully epitaxial r-GeO2/r-TiO2 heterostructure characterized by a more wavy but often facetted interface. items.title: Optical signatures of Rashba--Dresselhaus coupling across Franz--Keldysh and Landau regimes in two-dimensional semiconductors
items.abstract: We develop a unified theory of the interband optical response of a two-dimensional semiconductor with simultaneous Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit couplings in electric and magnetic fields. In crossed fields, the in-plane electric field generates an effective spin-orbit drift field that modifies the Landau spectrum and spinor states, while at zero magnetic field the problem maps onto Landau--Zener spin dynamics.At zero external fields, the total joint density of states above the band gap remains unchanged, while characteristic subgap structures appear. Pure Rashba coupling produces an inverse square root singularity, whereas a finite Dresselhaus term gives a step and a logarithmic peak, allowing the two couplings to be distinguished optically. At zero magnetic field, the Franz--Keldysh response shows a crossover from diabatic to adiabatic spin dynamics as the electric field is reduced....

items.title: NN-Based Transistor Modeling for Ultra-Fast SPICE Simulation and Standard Cell Library Characterization
items.abstract: Neural network (NN)-based transistor models have proven to be a promising solution to accelerate device modeling. Although these models demonstrated remarkable speedup in circuit simulations, they were not rigorously tested in complex tasks within standard EDA tool flows for chip design, which require very high transistor model precision to provide accurate results and converge properly. To investigate their full potential and promise, we develop NN-based transistor models that accurately predict the drain current and various charges for a 3nm nanosheet, and employ the models for a standard cell library characterization. This enables us to evaluate the accuracy and speedup under a very wide range of SPICE simulations, benchmarking our models against an industry-standard implementation. items.title: The Reaction of Financial Markets to the Releases of DeepSeek R1 and Kimi K3: A Critical Analysis
items.abstract: This paper compares financial-market reactions to the releases of DeepSeek R1 in January 2025 and Kimi K3 in July 2026. Both AI models were presented as credible Chinese competitors near the capability frontier, but their releases conveyed different economic information. DeepSeek R1 combined open weights with unusually low reported training and inference costs, prompting investors to reassess expected demand for computing infrastructure and producing large stock-price decreases among semiconductor and data-centre-related firms. Kimi K3 instead entered at broadly frontier prices and generated a market reaction concentrated more heavily among rival Chinese AI laboratories. items.title: Localization Contrast As a Fundamental Limit of Radiative Quantum Efficiency
items.abstract: Disorder can localize valence- and conduction-band states to different degrees, yet whether such localization contrast has observable consequences remains poorly understood. Here, we show that localization contrast strongly impacts competing carrier-recombination channels. We illustrate this behavior in random In$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N alloys. Increasing the In content from $x=13.5\%$ to $x=22\%$ progressively localizes the valence-band maximum state while leaving the conduction-band minimum state comparatively delocalized. This contrasting localization decreases the interband optical momentum matrix element underlying radiative recombination. For Auger-Meitner recombination, however, localization alone does not determine the coupling; atomic-scale disorder also breaks primitive-cell translational symmetry and modifies the momentum-space and phase structure of the states. items.title: Strain-induced structural transformations in hexagonal monolayer boron nitride. A density functional study
items.abstract: In this work we theoretically study the structural transformations occurring in monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) subjected to strong deformations. The first-principle computer simulations are based on the density functional theory employing the pseudopotentials with the exchange-correlation energy given in Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof form. Depending on the direction and the type of the strain, the simulations reveal different types of structural transformations in two-dimensional (2D) h-BN associated with the elastic failure. It is found that, under certain shear strains, there can form an ordered 2D orthorhombic phase with the 2D layer space symmetry pmmm. Thermal stability of the latter up to ~900 K is demonstrated by first-principle Born-Oppenheimer molecular dynamics. items.title: Electrically Pumped Quadratic-Soliton Mode-Locked Laser in Lithium Niobate Nanophotonics
items.abstract: Femtosecond mode-locked lasers are the workhorse of modern photonics, enabling optical atomic clocks, frequency combs, precision spectroscopy, and ultrafast signal processing. Bringing them onto nanophotonic chips promises miniaturized ultrafast systems, yet combining femtosecond pulse generation with electrical pumping remains a major challenge, rooted in a trade-off between the speed and energy efficiency of mode-locking mechanisms. Kerr-based mechanisms offer nearly instantaneous response but typically require high intracavity peak powers that are difficult to achieve with nanophotonic-compatible semiconductor gain. Conversely, semiconductor saturable absorbers enable strong nonlinear responses at low energies but are limited by their slow carrier dynamics. items.abstract: Recently, two-dimensional goldene, a single-atomic-layer gold sheet, has been experimentally realized and is expected to be a promising material for next-generation devices, offering new possibilities beyond three-dimensional bulk gold. Because quasi-one-dimensional derivatives can exhibit properties markedly different from their two-dimensional counterparts, we investigate the stability, electronic, and magnetic properties of goldene-based nanoribbons (GOLDNRs) using first-principles computational methods. Our findings demonstrate that the electronic structure of these nanoribbons depends strongly on both edge chirality and ribbon width. Depending on the boundary configuration, the systems can exhibit semiconducting behavior with electronic band gaps of approximately 0.77 eV and 0.04 eV, or retain metallic characteristics. items.title: HAWK: Heterogeneity-Aware KV Cache Transfer for Efficient GPU-NPU Phase-Disaggregated LLM Inference
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference exhibits distinct computational characteristics across its two phases: prefill is compute-intensive, whereas decode is more memory-bound. As a result, AI accelerators achieve varying levels of efficiency across the two phases. GPUs are well suited to prefill, but are often underutilized during decode. By contrast, NPUs can utilize their compute resources more effectively during decode. Motivated by this observation, we explore a heterogeneous architecture that integrates GPUs and NPUs, mapping prefill to GPUs and decode to NPUs to achieve high performance and efficiency. items.abstract: We observe novel optical fringes and emission coherence in laterally formed semiconductor fins using wavelength- and angle-resolved cathodoluminescence (WARCL). These findings demonstrate that cavity mode and emission confinement are directly governed by cavity geometry including cavity dimensions, facet angles, and orientation. In flat fins narrowing the width from 3000 nm to 200 nm sharpens fringe intensity, indicating stronger mode confinement and increased coherence. Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations confirm that the observed fringes originate from internal reflections among the fin facets, consistent with a Fabry-Pérot (FP) cavity model where the cavity length determines the fringe spacing. Here, we demonstrate that pronounced AMR can instead arise from the anisotropic magnetic-field-induced polarization of dilute local moments in paramagnetic Fe-doped Ta4SiTe4, a quasi-one-dimensional van der Waals narrow-gap semiconductor. Magnetization measurements reveal Curie-like paramagnetism down to 2 K, with the c axis as the magnetic easy axis. The magnetization is described by an effective S = 1/2 model with an anisotropic g-factor ratio of g_c/g_ab = 1.43(1). items.abstract: Exciton-polaritons (EPs) are valuable for investigating macroscopic quantum coherent phenomena. However, overcoming the rapid decoherence of EPs under ambient conditions is challenging, even using delicately fabricated optical cavities. Ultrafast two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy (2DES) resolves two types of quantum beating: Rabi oscillation with a period of ~ 24 fs and a slower, ~ 50 fs period oscillation, revealing coherent coupling not only between excitons and cavity, but also between polaritons and dark states. items.title: The Spectroscopic Atlas of Excitonic Complexes in hBN-Encapsulated S-TMD Monolayers: From Excitons to Oxcitons and Beyond
items.abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) encapsulation has transformed the optical spectroscopy of semiconducting transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayers (MLs) by suppressing extrinsic disorder and enabling the resolution of an increasingly complex hierarchy of excitonic states. This Review provides a spectroscopy-oriented framework for understanding and identifying excitonic complexes in hBN-encapsulated Mo- and W-based MLs and their alloys. The discussion covers bright and dark excitons, Rydberg states, charged excitons, biexcitons, phonon-assisted replicas, and higher-order Fermi-sea many-body states, including hexcitons and oxcitons, with an emphasis on the experimental signatures that distinguish them. Particular attention is given to the combined use of photoluminescence and absorption-related spectroscopy, electrostatic gating, polarization analysis, excitation-power and temperature depen...

items.title: Online Open-World Wafer Defect Discovery using Hyperdimensional Computing
items.abstract: Conventional wafer defect analysis relies on offline, closed-world classifiers that fail to detect novel, unseen defect signatures emerging during continuous semiconductor manufacturing. To address this, we propose WaferHDC, an online open-world wafer defect discovery framework based on hyperdimensional computing (HDC). The memory-centric architecture of WaferHDC enables rapid anomaly detection and grouping of recurring failures into compact hypervector representations. This allows the memory space to dynamically scale with new defect modes without retraining a static classifier or archiving entire raw wafer history. WaferHDC first models normal spatial distributions, then dynamically groups recurring failures into persistent defect memory without labels or predefined class counts. It outperforms the strongest online baseline by 13.3 p.p. in adjusted Rand index and 10.5 p.p. in normalize...

items.title: Ultrafast and Anisotropic Exciton Transport in Layered NbOI$_2$
items.abstract: Ferroelectric layered semiconductors provide a unique platform for exploring coupled excitonic and electronic phenomena in reduced dimensions. Here, exciton transport in layered NbOI$_2$ is investigated using transient absorption microscopy. Ultrafast and strongly anisotropic exciton diffusion is observed. The diffusion coefficient of about 160 cm$^2$ s$^{-1}$ along the nonpolar crystal axis is among the highest reported for van der Waals semiconductors. The transport exhibits an approximately twofold in-plane anisotropy between the polar and nonpolar directions, reflecting the intrinsic low-symmetry crystal structure of NbOI$_2$. The environmental stability of NbOI$_2$ is further investigated, and fabrication and encapsulation conditions required to achieve long-term sample stability are identified. items.title: Accelerating real-time hybrid-functional calculations with learned ACE and symmetry-based FFT reuse
items.abstract: Real-time hybrid-functional calculations require repeated reconstruction of nonlocal exchange, whose cost grows rapidly with Brillouin-zone sampling. We develop two methods to improve the efficiency of time evolution and spatial processing. The first learns the time evolution of adaptively compressed exchange (ACE) factors and predicts their updates, reducing the frequency of explicit reconstruction. The second uses crystal symmetry to reuse exchange fast Fourier transforms (FFTs) among equivalent real-space points. This symmetry-based FFT reuse (SBFR) reduces the number of FFTs while retaining the full $\bm k$-point sum. The methods can be used with a variety of hybrid functionals, and we use HSE06 in this work. items.title: Nanophotonic Extreme Ultraviolet Polarimeter
items.abstract: Nanophotonic engineering has revolutionized how we manipulate the polarization of visible light. Here, we extend such control to extreme ultraviolet radiation, the spectral region of attosecond science and semiconductor lithography, where transmissive optical elements are lacking. We implement channel waveguides that restrict incident 41-nm-wavelength light to a few modes with defined spatial profiles and propagation constants. By designing the propagation-length-dependent interference of two eigenmodes, we achieve polarization-dependent forward scattering, which we exploit to create a transmissive nanophotonic analyzer that resolves the polarization axis and spectrum of extreme ultraviolet light from a single measurement. items.abstract: Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides provide a promising material platform for optical phase manipulation, as rapid variations in their dielectric functions can give rise to topological phase singularities (PSs). However, PS evolution while preserving topological charge conservation has not yet been investigated in exciton enabled PS systems. Here, using atomically thin MoS2 films on sapphire as a model system, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate that the evolution of dielectric dispersion determines the creation, trajectory, merging, and annihilation of optical PSs under topological charge conservation. By varying the MoS2 film thickness, we experimentally realize this evolution through the gradual shrinking of the high energy n-k dispersion loop, which modifies its intersection with the zero reflection condition. items.title: Nanocrystalline cubic boron arsenide growth on GaAs(100) by gas source molecular beam epitaxy
items.abstract: Cubic boron arsenide (c-BAs) is a promising ultrahigh thermal conductivity semiconductor, but its direct synthesis on lattice-mismatched substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate the synthesis of nanocrystalline c-BAs thin films on GaAs(100) substrates using gas source molecular beam epitaxy. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy reveals an optimal growth temperature window of 250-400 C to maintain near stoichiometry and suppress severe arsenic loss. Surface and structural characterizations via atomic force microscopy, reflection high-energy electron diffraction, and grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction demonstrate a Volmer-Weber 3D island growth mode and a preferential crystallographic alignment with the GaAs substrate. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy confirms a chemically sharp interface without gallium interdiffusion into the c-BAs layer. These findings establish...

items.abstract: We demonstrate a multi-agent framework that takes an analog circuit from topology synthesis to layout. A researcher agent directs schematic and layout agents, a four-tier memory stores the specification and lessons, and separate agents review the designs. Deterministic tools provide pass/fail simulation reports, symbolic analysis, graph-based netlist equivalence, parasitic injection, and extraction with DRC and LVS in every optimization trial. A human approves the specification and the layout plan. For a fourth-order, 250-Hz subthreshold biopotential low-pass filter, the researcher agent synthesized, through simulation-guided trial and error, a novel current-reuse architecture that shares a single dc bias branch between a super-source-follower biquad and a flipped-voltage-follower biquad. items.abstract: Utility-scale quantum technologies will not only require a well-performing quantum platform, but also classical control hardware that is scalable, efficient, and meets the design requirements set by the quantum system of interest. One approach is the application of silicon CMOS technology, a highly scalable and mature technology, to design application-specific integrated circuits (ASIC) that are optimized for the quantum system. In this work, we present two-qubit control of electron and nuclear spins in NV centres in diamond, using a cryogenic CMOS qubit controller integrated with a diamond quantum device in a cryostat. Using Gate Set Tomography (GST) we characterize the performance of the single-qubit gates on both electron- and carbon nuclear spins, and analyze the limiting noise processes. Extracting reliable polarimetric signals requires rigorous observational calibration, spatial co-alignment, and noise reduction via stacking. We report optical linear polarimetric observations acquired during the 8 April 2024 total solar eclipse from Dallas, Texas, USA, near solar maximum. Using a full-frame color CMOS detector paired with an 80~mm refractor, multi-band Red, Green, and Blue (RGB) images were recorded simultaneously across three polarizer orientations ($-60^\circ$, $0^\circ$, and $+60^\circ$) using a 9-step exposure bracket ($1/800\text{~s}$ to $1/3\text{~s}$). items.title: Privacy-Preserving Robust Monitoring of Dense-Time Temporal Logic
items.abstract: Motivated by the use of third-party testing, this paper presents a privacy-preserving implementation of the robustness monitoring of Signal Temporal Logic (STL). STL is a specification language for systems whose output traces have real-valued timestamps -- most prominently, cyber-physical systems. Its robust semantics, which assign real rather than binary truth values, are an essential ingredient of systems testing and runtime monitoring. In a number of system testing scenarios, the designer and the tester are separate parties. This testing-as-a-service model is common in software, avionics, and semiconductors, and is growing in importance in the red-teaming of machine learning models. In such a model, the designer seeks to preserve the privacy (or secrecy) of its design, while the tester seeks to preserve the privacy of its collateral, including the detailed specification suite. This pa...

items.title: Anchored Exploration in Product Evolution: A Phylogenetic Network Framework for Semiconductor Designs
items.abstract: We develop a product phylogenetic network framework for examining anchored exploration. Using 102,465 semiconductor products grouped into 45,996 design families, we distinguish accumulated design continuity (Anchor) from externally precedented feature additions (horizontal transfer, HT). Fitted regressions yield non-monotonic relationships for HT occurrence and descendant carriage, alongside increasing within-family carriage over observed support. These patterns connect technological trajectories and recombination by distinguishing the continuity associated with incorporating external features from that associated with reproducing them in subsequent products.

A recent example is silicon oxynitride-doped silicon [2] discovered recently by our group, offering to set a new position for the fields of silicon photonics with a precise control of refractive index from 2.1 to 2.5 together with the photosensitivity property at different wavelengths. In this study, we demonstrate that the synthesis of silicon oxynitride-doped silicon can be performed on a flexible substrate for the fabrication of Bragg gratings (BG) at low temperatures below 100 degrees Celsius that are emerging for advanced applications. items.title: Superradiant temporal transition radiation of a relativistic electron beam
items.abstract: A charge in uniform motion carries a bound field that does not radiate. Transition radiation releases part of it at a boundary in space. We propose and analyze the case of radiation emission due to a boundary in time: a relativistic electron bunch passes through an aperture in a semiconductor (silicon) wafer, and while its bound field occupies the wafer, a femtosecond laser switches the semiconductor into an electron-hole plasma. The field is a valid solution of the old medium and not of the new one, so it is handed to the plasma as an initial condition for radiation emission at the plasma frequency. Because in temporal transition radiation (t-TR) the wavevector is conserved, and the frequency is not, the emission can appear in a spectral band that the bunch's own field does not populate. Every electron contributes in phase to the initial condition at the switching moment, so the emitted...

items.title: Molecular Doping of MoS$_2$ with N-Heterocyclic Carbenes: A Raman Study of Interfacial Charge Transfer
items.abstract: We demonstrate efficient electron doping of exfoliated MoS$_2$ through the deposition of N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) molecules onto its surface. Raman spectroscopy reveals a pronounced softening of the optical A$_{1g}$ phonon mode after NHC deposition, consistent with electron transfer from the NHC molecules to the MoS$_2$ layers. The largest phonon-energy shifts are observed in monolayer and bilayer flakes whereas changes in bulk-like MoS$_2$ are negligible, indicating that the doping efficiency depends on the number of layers. This thickness dependence highlights the dominant role of interfacial charge transfer at the NHC/MoS$_2$ interface. Quantitative analysis of the Raman modes of as-exfoliated and NHC-covered MoS$_2$, together with comparison with literature values, allows us to estimate an increase in the two-dimensional electron density of about two-orders of magnitude in MoS$_2...

items.title: Epitaxial Displacement-etched GaAsSb Quantum Dots Emitting at Telecom Wavelengths
items.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are essential components for integrated photonic and quantum information systems, yet current epitaxial growth techniques face significant limitations in complexity of growth, material selection, and density tunability. Here we report a displacement etch technique that enables controlled formation of GaAsSb QDs with emission at telecommunications wavelengths. Our approach uses arsenic molecular flux (As$_2$) to react with antimonide surfaces through thermodynamically favorable displacement reactions, creating three-dimensional quantum confined nanostructures without requiring strain-driven growth or complex droplet-based processes. Density functional theory shows the two competing As-for-Sb exchange pathways to be nearly equivalent in both reaction energy and activation barrier, which places morphological control in the subsequent adatom kinetics rather t...

items.title: Concatenated continuous-drive protection of exchange-based spin-qubit gates
items.abstract: Exchange-based two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits are sensitive to low-frequency detuning noise and control errors. Here, we extend concatenated continuous driving (CCD), implemented by phase modulation of a global microwave drive, to exchange-based SWAP and $\sqrt{\mathrm{SWAP}}$ operations between double-dressed spin qubits and investigate its effectiveness for protecting two-qubit gates. We find that CCD retains strong protection against quasistatic common-mode detuning errors while substantially improving robustness against Rabi-frequency errors and qubit-to-qubit Rabi-frequency mismatch compared with conventional continuous dressing. By contrast, the gate fidelity is impacted by differential detuning errors. By modeling partially correlated quasistatic detuning noise, we further show that the noise-averaged gate fidelity depends strongly on the spatial correlation of the q...

items.title: Water-Driven Porous Silicon as a Platform for Blue Materials
items.abstract: Living organisms control water to transport matter, transfer energy and drive chemical reactions. In this perspective, we argue that porous silicon can give engineering materials comparable control over water. Its pore architecture, surface chemistry and semiconducting skeleton can be shaped across length scales with the precision of semiconductor processing and, like the water it can host, it relies on one of the most abundant chemical elements on Earth. Liquids in porous silicon, most often water, can flow as a continuum through pores a few nanometers wide, strain the skeleton through capillary and electrosorption stresses, shift structural color, switch transparency, and modulate or generate electrical signals. We describe three directions to combine and extend these effects and overcome their limitations. Pore hierarchy resolves the classical trade-off between interface area and tran...

items.title: Gate-defined quantum dot and charge noise analysis in a Forksheet transistor
items.abstract: We report the cryogenic characterization of a 14-nm nMOS Forksheet transistor down to 10 mK. We demonstrate that the device retains transistor operation with improved characteristics at cryogenic temperatures, while also forming a gate-defined quantum dot that can be tuned to the single-electron regime. In the quantum-dot regime, we perform low-frequency charge-noise measurements across different charge occupations and observe an average charge-noise amplitude of $\langle S_0\rangle = 10\;μ\mathrm{eV}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ at 1 Hz, with a minimum measured value of $3.3\;μ\mathrm{eV}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$. These results highlight the potential of Forksheet technology for the monolithic cointegration of quantum and classical CMOS functionalities in future quantum processors.

items.title: Revealing Detailed Transport Mechanisms in Silicon Tunneling Diodes
items.abstract: Understanding carrier transport in heavily doped semiconductor junctions is essential for developing next-generation tunneling devices for cryogenic electronics and steep-slope technologies. In this work, we investigate the transport mechanisms in a silicon tunneling diode using extensive TCAD (Technology Computer Aided Design) simulations benchmarked against electrical measurements over a wide temperature range of 4 K to 440 K. The measured device characteristics show no negative differential conductance, strong temperature dependence of forward current with a nearly constant semi-logarithmic slope, and weak temperature dependence under high reverse bias. To identify the mechanisms underlying these characteristics, we investigate the contributions of band-to-band tunneling (BTBT), trap-assisted tunneling (TAT), Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) recombination, and avalanche generation. items.title: Engineering nonrelativistic spin splitting in semiconductors by altermagnetic proximity
items.abstract: Altermagnets combine vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting, offering functionalities attractive for spintronics and quantum devices. Their practical use, however, is constrained by the limited availability of materials that simultaneously possess the required altermagnetic symmetry, semiconducting electronic structure, and weak spin-orbit coupling. Here we show that these requirements can instead be separated between constituent materials through proximity engineering. We develop an analytical theory for a conventional semiconductor coupled to a gapped $d$-wave altermagnet and demonstrate that virtual tunneling transfers the altermagnetic spin splitting to the semiconductor. Yet assessments commonly examine them separately, limiting our understanding of where resource pressures arise, how they are transferred across space, and who bears their consequences. items.abstract: Single-crystal diamond membranes (SCDms) were created using a hydrogen ion-cut process combined with a two-step post-implantation annealing, electrochemical etching, and micro-transfer printing. After delamination and removal of residual graphitic material, freestanding SCDms with improved crystalline quality were obtained. items.title: From quantum emitters to technological platforms: a perspective on semiconductor quantum dots
items.abstract: Photonic quantum technologies are based on controlled photon states. To generate these, quantum dots have emerged as excellent sources of single and entangled photons. In this Perspective, we briefly review the chronological development of quantum dots as photon sources, from their beginnings as quantum emitters in the early 2000s to the advanced photonic devices being developed today. We highlight the interplay between fundamental research and industrial aspects before discussing the photonic quantum technologies we expect to emerge in the near future.

items.title: From Surface Reactions to Inhibitor Coverage: A Machine-Learning-Assisted Computational Study of Area-Selective Atomic Layer Deposition
items.abstract: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) enables selective material growth for the fabrication of nanoscale semiconductor devices. Predicting inhibitor coverage is essential for understanding and optimizing surface blocking in AS-ALD. Here, we present a computational workflow combining a pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potential with off-lattice grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations and apply it to inhibitor adsorption and precursor blocking on amorphous SiO2. Realistic surface models reveal substantial site-dependent variations in reaction energies and activation barriers, with silanol groups serving as the primary adsorption sites for aminosilane and related inhibitors and metal precursors. Coverage simulations show that inhibitors producing identical adsorbed fragments can yield different coverages because the intact molecules impose distinct steric constrai...

items.title: Coherent phonons in photoexcited semiconductors from first principles
items.abstract: Coherent phonons are phase-locked lattice vibrations that provide a sensitive probe of nonequilibrium dynamics in materials. Existing first-principles equation-of-motion (EOM) approaches have successfully described coherent phonons in metals and semimetals, but their extension to semiconductors requires treating the long-lived electron--hole plasma created by above-gap excitation. Here we extend the first-principles EOM framework to photoexcited semiconductors by incorporating the residual plasma force that shifts the lattice equilibrium together with the plasma-induced renormalization of the electronic structure. For monolayer MoTe$_2$, the calculated carrier-density-dependent Te displacement agrees with constrained density-functional perturbation theory only when the renormalized band structure is included. We then show that increasing the photoexcited carrier density enhances both the...

items.title: Programmable Preparation of Topological Entangled States
items.abstract: Programmable preparation of entangled quantum states is a central requirement for scalable quantum information processing, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing. Topological photonic platforms offer an attractive route towards robust quantum-state generation by encoding information in symmetry- protected optical modes, yet the generated entangled states are typically dictated by the lattice geometry and therefore lack programmability. Here we demonstrate programmable preparation of topological entangled states by inverse engineering the nonlinear optical pump profile of an integrated photonic lattice. Our approach enables deterministic control over both the dimensionality and modal structure of the generated entangled state while preserving its topological character. We experimentally realize silicon photonic topological superlattices in which the nonlinear generation pathway...

items.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
items.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $μ$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

items.title: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moiré Hubbard bands
items.abstract: Moiré semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. The ESM is in the clean limit, persists down to about 50mK, and spans over multiple symmetry-breaking ground states; it also appears only at small twist angles, where electronic correlations are strong. These observations distinguish the state from the reported strange...

items.title: Energetics of Fault-Tolerant Spin-Qubit Quantum Computation
items.abstract: Semiconductor spin qubits offer a promising route to compact and scalable quantum computers, combining long coherence times in isotopically purified silicon with compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing. Beyond computational speedup, their energy efficiency is an important consideration for future large-scale systems. We evaluate the power and energy requirements of a Loss-DiVincenzo spin-qubit quantum computer by analyzing the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) and benchmarking it against the classical Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). We develop a detailed energy budget, identifying cryogenic cooling as the dominant baseline contribution before quantum error correction (QEC). The comparison between the QFT and the classical FFT reveals that, for any quantum workload operating under a polynomially bounded sampling regime, the crossover in energy consumption occurs at smaller problem size...

items.title: A Decade In, zeroRISC Sees A Bright Future For Open Silicon
Low magnon damping of a EuSe film down to millikelvin temperatures
items.abstract: The rapid development of quantum magnonics over the past decade has created a demand for magnetic materials that keep their magnon losses low at millikelvin temperatures and add functionality beyond that of the established iron garnets and ferromagnetic metals. The europium chalcogenides are natural candidates $-$ they are magnetic semiconductors whose moment of $7\,μ_{\mathrm{B}}$ per Eu$^{2+}$ ion stems from a half-filled $4f$ shell with zero orbital momentum, so that spin-orbit coupling and intrinsic damping are expected to be weak. Here we characterize an epitaxial film of the metamagnet EuSe on diamagnetic BaF$_2$ by magnetometry and broadband ferromagnetic resonance from 10 K down to 30 mK. EuSe combines a saturation magnetization of 1100 kA/m with antiferromagnetic, ferrimagnetic and ferromagnetic phases that are reached with fields below 0.25 T. In contrast to a Gilbert-damped fe...

items.title: Novel high-pressure silicon allotrope with quartz topology from first principles
items.abstract: A novel silicon allotrope, qtz Si, with quartz topology is proposed and investigated alongside four known allotropes (dia Si-I, lon Si-IV, bsn Si-II, and gsi Si-III) using first-principles density functional theory. qtz Si is found to exhibit the smallest atom-averaged volume (18.06 A3), highest density (2.582 g/cm3), highest bulk modulus (98 GPa), and highest maximum phonon frequency (16 THz) among the five, while showing the lowest shear modulus (37 GPa). All five allotropes are confirmed to satisfy the Born stability criteria and to display positive phonon frequencies throughout the Brillouin zone, i.e., they are mechanically and dynamically stable. Electronic structure calculations show that qtz Si is a semimetal with a vanishing gap, whereas dia Si and lon Si are semiconductors, and bsn and gsi allotropes are weakly metallic. items.abstract: Many-body perturbation theory (MBPT) methods, including the GW approximation, the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW-BSE) method, and GW perturbation theory (GWPT), among others, provide accurate first-principles descriptions of excited-state properties and multiparticle interactions of materials. However, their use remains limited due to complex multi-software workflows, interdependent physical parameters, and substantial theoretical expertise. Large language model (LLM) agents, which couple a language model to software tools, show potential in automating computational tasks, but MBPT remains an unaddressed challenge. We show that LLM agents tested in our work, including frontier models such as Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5, do not reliably construct MBPT workflows in one attempt, suggesting that correct setup requires expert knowledge and consistency that current models lack. items.title: Robust Data-Driven Controller Synthesis from Sampled and Uncertain Frequency Response Estimates using Integral Quadratic Constraints
items.abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel MIMO controller synthesis method that relies solely on frequency-domain data of discrete-time systems. The approach is based on an iterative design procedure using \emph{integral quadratic constraints} (IQCs). It generalizes existing data-driven methods that approximate semi-infinite IQC conditions by enforcing them on a finite set of measured frequency points. Such approximations do not provide guarantees on the continuous frequency axis and may fail to capture inter-frequency behavior. We address this limitation by formulating a convex optimization problem that preserves robustness guarantees over the entire frequency range. In particular, the proposed method explicitly accounts for inter-frequency behavior of both plant and controller, leading to certified robust stability and performance. items.title: The Reciprocal tau-Cell: A Log-Domain Circuit for On-Chip Learning
items.abstract: Training hardware by gradient descent requires a gradient to be computed using a separate backwards pass. If a circuit is reciprocal, meaning every connection is symmetric, the backward pass is the same network run a second time with the error as its input. The reciprocal tau-cell, a weak-inversion log-domain circuit, makes this practical in standard CMOS. Each cell is a current-mode leaky integrator with a built-in ReLU; each connection is two transistors whose signed strength is a ratio of bias currents. The equilibrium of the network is the solution to a convex program, and latching the cells that are off will hardware linearise the circuit, making its second run exactly linear. Transistor-level SKY130 simulations show that the second run gives the gradient within 1.9%; that hardware linearisation permits large, noise-robust error signals; that a 13-cell network learns the Iris data s...

items.title: On-sky performance and prospects of near-infrared CMOS detectors in exoplanet detection: first year of SPIRIT
items.abstract: Ultracool dwarfs are promising targets for detecting and characterising temperate terrestrial exoplanets. Their flux peaks in the near-infrared, beyond the wavelength cut-off of the silicon-based CCDs used by ground-based surveys dedicated to observing them, such as SPECULOOS. We present the on-sky performance of SPIRIT (SPeculoos InfraRed Imager for Transits), an InGaAs CMOS detector on the Callisto telescope at the SPECULOOS Southern Observatory, during its first year of operation, from mid-2022 to 2023. We use 328 visits of 73 targets to optimise our CMOS-specific reduction process, including our approach to glow effects and bad-pixel handling. We find the measured precision to be consistent with our theoretical noise model, achieving sub-part-per-thousand precision under good observing conditions across targets spanning $J$-band magnitudes of 10--13. items.title: CAFE: Conducting-Cell-Aware Adaptive Differential Encoding for Robust DNN Inference in FeFET-Based Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET)-based compute-in-memory (CIM) promises energy-efficient deep neural network (DNN) inference, but device variation can severely degrade bit-sliced CIM accuracy. Prior works either rely on hardware modifications or treat such variation as generic noise, overlooking a key FeFET asymmetry: negligible off-state leakage makes errors dominated by conducting on-state cells. This asymmetry is amplified by two's-complement sign extension, which maps small negative values to high-significance bit slices and magnifies their errors during shift-and-add reconstruction. In this paper, we propose CAFE, a conducting-cell-aware adaptive differential encoding framework built upon this FeFET-specific asymmetry. CAFE introduces C$^2$AM, a bit-significance-weighted conducting-cell activity metric that predicts output deviation and inference accuracy degradation un...

items.title: Pressure engineering of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape and exciton-charge interplay in semiconductor moiré superlattices
items.abstract: Semiconductor moiré superlattices, owing to strongly bound excitons and pronounced electronic correlation, have emerged as an intriguing solid platform for exploring correlated bosonic phenomena, where the moiré potential landscape plays a central role. Hydrostatic pressure allows continuous, in-situ tuning of this landscape, but remains underexplored because of experimental challenges. Here we integrate a diamond anvil pressure cell with high quality dual gated WSe2/WS2 twisted bilayers and perform cryogenic optical spectroscopy. We observe distinct pressure evolutions of moiré intralayer excitons, which reveal drastic modulation of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape captured by a continuum model and suggest the capability of engineering the exciton-band topology. items.abstract: We propose CktHGVAE, a heterogeneous graph variational autoencoder for transistor-level analog/mixedsignal CMOS circuits that takes not only design variables but also state variables as its inputs and outputs. With a single hyperparameter configuration without topology-specific tuning, comparison between model-generated and SPICE-simulated circuit operational states gives median R2 values above 0.9 for typical single-ended voltage amplifiers and the CMOS inverter, and 0.81-0.96 for differential amplifiers with larger datasets. Latent-space optimization in the PCA-reduced latent space with Bayesian optimization, evolutionary search, random search, and quasi-exhaustive search is demonstrated for a common-source voltage amplifier with NMOS input and resistive load, where the objective function is defined as a penalty for deviation from required circuit specifications. items.abstract: Tracing my scientific path from many-body physics in semiconductor nanostructures to topological quantum matter, this Habilitation à diriger des recherches (HDR) memoir presents only part of my research since defending two PhD theses in Toulouse and Nizhny Novgorod in 2011. Focusing on pseudo-relativistic fermions and topological states in zinc-blende semiconductors and their heterostructures, it highlights my independent research program: identifying physical problems, developing predictive theories, and initiating new directions with experimentalists. The first part addresses Kane fermions in bulk HgCdTe: temperature-driven band inversion, domain-wall states, the collapse of Landau levels in crossed electric and magnetic fields, and disorder-induced topological transitions. items.abstract: Strong coupling between mobile charge carriers or excitons and lattice vibrations gives rise to polarons: quasiparticles formed by charge carriers dressed by a cloud of phonon excitations. Polaron formation determines transport properties of systems ranging from transition-metal oxides and organic semiconductors to light-harvesting complexes. In excitonic systems that admit a hard-core boson description, mapping the excitations to pseudospins provides a natural framework for studying polaron physics, including the nonperturbative regime in which hopping amplitudes, phonon energies, and coupling strengths are comparable. Here, we propose a trapped-ion blueprint for realizing spin-phonon Hamiltonians with programmable spatial coupling between excitation density and phonon displacements, encompassing local Holstein and long-range Fröhlich-type interactions. items.title: Single anyons and anyon binding in a quantum Hall dot
items.abstract: Anyons are particles with quantized fractional statistics. In theory, a single anyon can be stabilized as a localized fractional charge within the bulk of a topologically ordered two-dimensional insulator. However, experiments to date have focused on probing anyons in structures in which many anyonic excitations coexist and interact. Here, we demonstrate the trapping of a single anyon in a device consisting of a graphene-based quantum point contact with an embedded tunable quantum Hall dot. Benchmarking our device at v = 1, we demonstrate backscattering between Fermi liquid edge states mediated by the whole-electron Coulomb blockade of the dot. The cleanliness and control available in our device allow depletion of the dot to the last quasihole, and we observe spin blockade for transitions to the opposite-spin Landau level. items.abstract: Programming abstractions have traditionally been designed for humans, but code generation is increasingly performed by models and autonomous agents. We investigate abstractions for machine-driven programming through GPU and AI-accelerator kernel generation. items.title: Theory of exciton-exciton interactions with nontrivial electronic bands
items.abstract: Excitons are bound electron-hole pairs in semiconductors whose interactions influence optical properties and determine their collective behavior and emergent correlated phases. items.title: Evolution and breakdown of chiral anomaly in Weyl semiconductor tellurium
items.abstract: Chiral anomaly in topological materials manifests as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, yet the tunability and evolution of this effect remain elusive. Here we show that doped tellurium serves as a versatile platform to realize a giant negative longitudinal magnetoresistance that is highly tunable via the Fermi level and magnetic field. By moving the Fermi level towards the Weyl point, we observe a pronounced enhancement of negative magnetoresistance, which arises from chiral anomaly and robustly persists up to ambient temperature. Beyond the quantum limit, the system exhibits positive linear magnetoconductance, serving as a compelling transport signature of the chiral anomaly in the lowest Landau level. items.title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
items.abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for NV- decoherence in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters invert that attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.1-7.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies, over three decades of concentration. A bath dephases the qubit because its spins exchange spin projections with one another, and two can exchange only if their transition frequencies match. A fine-structure splitting shifts...

items.title: Device contacts as spin-state selectors for silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
items.abstract: Optically addressable defect spins in semiconductors are promising building blocks for scalable quantum technologies. Yet, the consequences of conventional contact schemes used in semiconductor device integration for the quantum spin environment remain largely unexplored. Using the silicon vacancy (V$_\mathrm{Si}$) in silicon carbide (SiC) as a model system, we show that a widely used contact metal, nickel (Ni), intrinsically perturbs the defect spin state and quenches the characteristic emission from the spin-quartet channel of V$_\mathrm{Si}$. Low-energy muon spin rotation further reveals that Ni contacts create a magnetically contaminated region extending at least $\sim$110 nm into the SiC, in stark contrast to non-magnetic contacts such as Ti and Al. items.title: A semiconductor photon-pair source based on a polariton cascade
items.abstract: We present a theoretical study of a semiconductor photon-pair source based on a radiative cascade enabled by a permanent exciton dipole. The source consists of a GaAs quantum dot placed between a metal nanoparticle and a mirror. The dot exciton and the localized electromagnetic mode mix to form upper and lower polaritons. Without a permanent dipole, a symmetry separating states with even and odd excitation numbers forbids photon emission between the polaritons. Separation of the mean electron and hole positions gives the exciton a permanent dipole and breaks this symmetry. The upper polariton can then emit an idler photon as it decays to the lower polariton. The lower polariton can emit a signal photon as the system returns to its ground state. Using an effective model, we calculate the probability that a prepared upper polariton emits both photons through the metal antenna. We also anal...

items.title: Accelerating Periodic Coupled Cluster and Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction Theories With Frozen Natural Orbitals

The approach includes conventional ground-state FNOs together with state-specific (SS-FNO) and state-averaged (SA-FNO) variants constructed from perturbative one-particle density matrices. We implement these approximations for periodic Moller-Plesset perturbation theory, algebraic diagrammatic construction, and equation-of-motion coupled cluster methods in the PySCF software package and benchmark them for correlation energies, equations of state, fundamental band gaps, and quasiparticle band structures of semiconductors and insulators. items.title: JANUS: A Multi-modal Foundation Neural Sampler for Disordered Materials
items.abstract: Disordered materials are central to modern technologies, from high-performance alloys to quantum devices, yet understanding and designing them requires exploring an enormous space of compositions and atomic arrangements. Here we introduce JANUS, a multimodal neural sampler that jointly explores chemical composition, atomic structure and volume, learning directly from the energy of the system without requiring pre-generated equilibrium configurations. Across test systems, JANUS reproduces reference equilibrium properties and recovers free energy and phase behavior with about three orders of magnitude fewer energy evaluations than reference Monte Carlo sampling. In multicomponent alloys, JANUS reproduces experimentally observed local chemical order and can be steered to further enhance chemical order and stiffness. items.title: On-chip nanoplasma for adaptive electromagnetic protection
items.abstract: Over the past decade, semiconductor diodes have served as the primary switching elements in adaptive electromagnetic (EM) protection, yet their performance has been compromised by parasitic effects and thermal accumulation, rendering them inadequate against the rapidly evolving landscape of high-power microwave (HPM) threats. Here we show that on-chip nanoplasma switches (NPMS), composed of gallium nitride electrodes on silicon carbide substrates, exhibit superior radio frequency (RF) and thermal characteristics, positioning them as ideal field-driven switches in RF front-end protectors. By integrating NPMS into metasurfaces, antennas and circuit limiters, we achieve an adaptive response that ensures low-loss transmission for normal signals and high shielding against HPMs, while offering extended operating bandwidth and substantially higher tolerance than conventional solid-state devices...

items.title: Odd-even dichotomy in the waveforms of modified Emden oscillators of arbitrary integer power
items.abstract: Closed-form waveforms of the modified Emden oscillators $\ddot x+(q+2)kx^q\dot x+k^2x^{2q+1}+ω^2x=0$ of arbitrary natural power $q$, and of their damped $c$-deformed versions, are obtained through a generalized commutative factorization that reduces them to Bernoulli equations. We show that commutative factorizations of Liénard equations are gauge-conjugated forms of the nonlocal linearizing transformation of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Kundu and Lakshmanan, the factorization constant being half the difference of the roots of the associated linear oscillator. These oscillators display an odd--even dichotomy: for odd $q$ they are isochronous, with period $2π/ω$ independent of the amplitude, within an explicitly bounded range of the integration constant, while for even $q$ the oscillations decay algebraically, as $t^{-1/q}$. items.title: Strain engineering of transient exciton diffusion in WSe2 monolayers at cryogenic temperatures
items.abstract: Tungsten-based transition metal dichalcogenides exhibit dark excitons as the energetically lowest states. These are crucial for exciton thermalization and propagation and they dominate low-temperature photoluminescence via the emergence of pronounced phonon sidebands. After a resonant excitation, highly mobile hot dark excitons are formed, which quickly thermalize into an equilibrium distribution. The application of strain modifies the exciton energy landscape and, in particular, the relative energy separation between bright and dark exciton states. The impact of strain on the transient photoluminescence and diffusion of non-equilibrium excitons has remained largely unexplored so far. items.abstract: Photonic reservoir computing is a promising physical machine-learning approach for time-series prediction. Quantization of the reservoir response signal is an important consideration in the implementation of photonic reservoir computing, and the number of quantization bits and sampling frequency need to be optimized to achieve high prediction performance and low energy consumption. In this study, we introduce the concept of approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser by quantizing the reservoir node states and output weights. items.title: Photon-conserving Raman soliton attractors in focusing and defocusing Kerr media
items.abstract: The sign of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient has long been regarded as irrelevant to the direction of the Raman-induced soliton self-frequency shift. Yet the standard generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) predicts a frequency shift that depends on the sign of the nonlinearity, which leads to an unphysical blue shift in the defocusing case. We resolve this inconsistency by deriving the time-domain form of the photon-conserving GNLSE (pcGNLSE) from its established frequency-domain counterpart. The derivation reveals that photon-number conservation imposes two sign modifications relative to the standard GNLSE: the Raman-shift coefficient acquires the absolute value of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient in place of its signed counterpart, and the self-steepening-Raman dissipation term likewise carries an absolute-value prefactor rather than a signed one. items.title: High-Fidelity Synthetic Transmission Electron Microscopy Image Generation Using Diffusion Probabilistic Models for Data-Limited Semiconductor Metrology
items.abstract: Advanced semiconductor nodes drastically increased demand for Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), yet destructive sample preparation, slow imaging and high costs severely limit the availability of diverse datasets needed for downstream machine learning (ML). Synthetic data generation is becoming essential, but current generative models often miss TEM-specific noise, structural detail, and stochastic variability crucial for evaluation. We present a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) framework for synthetic TEM image generation under extreme data scarcity. A progressive patch-based training strategy scales from low-resolution patches to full images, enabling from-scratch training with only 15 samples. items.title: Absorption and Phase-Contrast Microtomography Using Direct X-Ray Detection With Commercial Off-The-Shelf CMOS Sensors
items.abstract: This work presents high-resolution X-ray microtomography based on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) CMOS image sensors as direct detectors. The system uses a microfocus X-ray source in cone-beam geometry, enabling both absorption-contrast imaging, thanks to the sensor s intrinsic resolution, and phase-contrast imaging, by adjusting the object-to-sensor distance. A dynamic flat-field correction algorithm mitigates radiation-induced sensor degradation during long acquisitions. The setup provides voxel sizes from 3.9 microns to 5.2 microns, with an effective spatial resolution (FWHM) as fine as 9.6 microns in magnified phase-contrast mode (1.33x) and 21 microns in non-magnified absorption-contrast mode. Phase contrast enhances visualization of soft tissue boundaries that are difficult to visualize using absorption-contrast imaging in the same experimental configuration.

items.title: Exciton-Tunable Phase Control and Superstrong Coupling Through Multimode Polariton Engineering in Planar Waveguides
items.abstract: Strong light-matter coupling in optical waveguides provides a versatile platform for engineering hybrid polaritonic modes and their dispersion. Here we investigate multimode exciton-photon coupling in visible semiconductor waveguides supporting several transverse electric modes. Using rigorous coupled-wave analysis combined with a coupled-oscillator model, we show that the photonic band structure can be engineered across a range of regimes, from conventional multimode strong coupling to the superstrong coupling regime, where the Rabi splitting becomes comparable to the spacing between adjacent photonic modes. In the latter regime, hybridization between orthogonal electromagnetic modes is enabled by restricting the active material to a subregion of the mode volume where the photonic modes exhibit strong mutual overlap. items.title: Energy Consumption in Next Generation Radio Access Networks
items.abstract: Historically, in macro-cell-based networks, the radio access network (RAN) portion accounts for the largest share of energy consumption in mobile networks. With greater densification, the transition to small cells and increased virtualization of the radio processing functions, the relative energy use of the different network segments is changing. At the same time, open radio access networks (O-RAN) have emerged as a promising approach to support this evolution through open interfaces that enable a multi-vendor environment, support for hierarchical intelligent controls, and simplified, cost-effective radio units that facilitate large-scale deployments. This paper examines the impact of these changes on energy consumption in next-generation RAN architectures through transaction-based energy models.
